# Kern tabs — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for Kern tabs when content splits into tabbed panels: the one tab strip with primary and secondary levels over a data contract. `items` are data — value, label, optional content, disabled, leading icon and badge — so the strip and its panels come from one declaration, and `variant` picks the Material 3 level: primary under the app bar, secondary inside content, never both in one bar. Vertical orientation fills the active tab as a pill, which is the settings pattern, while `children` replaces the panel area with a caller-composed panel and per-item content is then ignored. The strip is a tablist with tabs and tabpanels rather than a styled button row — each tab points at its panel, only the active panel mounts so hidden panels never enter the tab order, and the tablist is one stop through roving tabindex. An empty or fully-disabled item list renders no tablist at all rather than an empty one, and there is no nesting and no lazy prop: a second level is a second strip, and keeping panel state across visits is the panel's own job. Fewer than three choices is a segmented button instead — tabs own tabbed content with panels.

## Native

### Features

Reach for Kern tabs when content splits into tabbed panels: the one tab strip with primary and secondary levels over a data contract — the native twin under the same contract. `items` are data — value, string label, optional content, disabled, leading icon and badge — so the strip and its panels come from one declaration, and `variant` picks the Material 3 level: primary under the app bar, secondary inside content, never both in one bar. Vertical orientation stacks the tabs with the active tab filling as a pill, which is the settings pattern, while `children` replaces the panel area with a caller-composed panel and per-item content is then ignored. Tabs render with tablist and tab roles reporting selected state, each tab its own stop with the panel following the press, and only the active panel shows. An empty or fully-disabled item list renders no tablist at all rather than an empty one, and there is no nesting and no lazy prop: a second level is a second strip, and keeping panel state across visits is the panel's own job.
